chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Hafs ibn Umar, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
High prices worsen the manners, remove the trustworthiness, and wear out the magnanimity of the Muslim.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and social effects of high prices in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the economic phenomenon of inflation directly to spiritual decay, noting that excessive pricing corrupts character (akhlaq) and erodes trustworthiness (amanah). This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding how market dynamics influence individual morality and social cohesion, emphasizing that greed in trade is not merely a financial issue but a moral failing that isolates the believer from the community.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahman Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Hafs Bin Umar, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The high prices worsens the manners, and removes the trustworthiness, and wears out the magnanimity of the Muslim’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il al-Sarraj from Hafs ibn ‘Umar from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
High prices worsens moral discipline, destroy trust and cause suffering to the Muslims.’”
